title: Evaluation context
description: The members that the protocol adds to the member context of an AuthZEN 1.0 evaluation. Merge them into the context of a request and into the context of a response. A receiver ignores each member that it does not know. The root schema accepts the context of a request and of a response. The members $defs.request_context and $defs.answer_context are stricter. A schema cannot check that a ceiling is declared.

usage.description: In a request: the units of one use (protocol 6.4). In an answer: the units that the PDP took (protocol 6.12).

limits.description: In a true answer: the ceilings that apply (protocol 7.3). It holds ceilings only. A budget value never appears in an answer.

match.description: In a request: node, the default, or subtree (protocol 4.4).

approval.description: In a request: the effect of the operation, for the use of an action that has the member approval (protocol 17.1). The question never has op or view.

evaluation_id.description: In a false answer with the reason approval_required or approval_pending, for a question with an effect: a text that only the PDP reads (protocol 17.1). The PEP sends it back in the submission of a request (protocol 17.4).

reason.description: In a false answer: the reason (protocol 11.1). The values that the protocol gives are unknown_subject, invalid_resource, invalid_request, approval_required, approval_pending, approval_denied, approval_expired and budget_exceeded. A PEP maps another text as a false answer with no reason (protocol 10.3).

retry_after.description: In a false answer with the reason budget_exceeded: the seconds to wait, a whole number from 1 (protocol 11.1).

effect.description: The effect of an operation: the text sha256: and 64 lower-case hexadecimal digits (protocol 17.3).

request_context.description: The context of a question. The units are 1 (protocol 6.4). A question with usage has no match equal to subtree (protocol 6.11).

answer_context.description: The context of an answer. The reason budget_exceeded comes with retry_after (protocol 11.1).
